How it works

Three steps. No chasing, no awkward Venmo requests.

Built for one-time jobs — a website, a freelance gig, a single invoice — where you want to be paid as a business, not as a person in someone's contacts list.

STEP 01

Name the payment

Set the amount and what it's for below. The payee name is locked in as Panther Secure Pay — that's what appears on the checkout page, the receipt, and the client's card statement.

STEP 02

Send one secure link

Copy the ready-made message and send it however you like. Your client pays by card on an encrypted checkout — no sign-up, no app, and no bank details changing hands.

STEP 03

Get paid like a business

The money lands in your bank account, the client gets a proper receipt under the Panther Secure Pay name, and the job is closed out cleanly. Rename it for the next job whenever you want.

Why it's secure

Quiet, watchful, and very hard to rob.

A panther doesn't leave anything valuable lying around — and neither do we. Every payment runs through encrypted, processor-handled checkout.

  • ✓
    Your real name stays off it

    Checkout pages, receipts, and card statements show “Panther Secure Pay.” Your personal name never appears to the client.

  • ✓
    Card details never touch you

    Payments are processed by a PCI-compliant provider. You never see, hold, or store a card number — and neither does the panther.

  • ✓
    One link, one job

    Each link is made for a single payment. When the job's done, the link's done — rename the entity or spin up a fresh one anytime.

  • ✓
    A paper trail both sides trust

    Instant receipts, a clear statement descriptor, and a record of every payment — so there's never a “wait, who did I pay?” moment.

Questions

Asked often, answered once

Is “Panther Secure Pay” the name clients actually see?

Yes. That's the whole point. The checkout page, email receipt, and card-statement line all read Panther Secure Pay. Your legal name stays in your account settings, where only you and the payment processor can see it.

Can I change the name for the next transaction?

Yes — the display name isn't permanent. Change it in your payment settings whenever you like, and the next link, receipt, and statement will use the new name. Per-transaction statement suffixes are also possible on API-created checkouts.

What does it cost to receive a payment?

Standard card processing is estimated at 2.9% + 30¢ per payment in the builder above — so a $600 payment nets about $582.30. There are no monthly fees for a simple payment link, and the client pays nothing extra.

Do I actually have to pay a panther?

The panther is the brand, the payee name, and the head of collections. Whether a portion of proceeds goes toward snacks for Bagheera is between you and Bagheera. He recommends yes.

What do clients need in order to pay?

Just the link and a card (or Apple Pay / Google Pay). No account, no app download, no bank details shared with you — they check out in under a minute and get a receipt instantly.
